chunks: I gave you my orders at Mun‘araji’l-liwã but you did not see the good of my counsel till the noon of next day (when it was too late).

key_terms.ضُحَى: Late morning, specifically the time when the sun has risen and reached a certain height, often used to denote a time after the early morning.
key_terms.مُنْعَرَجِ اللِّوَى: A place name, specifically the turning point or bend of the flag, referring to the location at Siffin where Ali's army turned back.

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of Mun‘araji’l-liwã in Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: This poetic verse, often cited in the context of the Battle of Siffin, highlights the delay in the Sahaba's (companions') full comprehension of Ali ibn Abi Talib’s strategic command, which was given at Munzarq al-Lawwa (a specific location near Damascus). It underscores a key Shia scholarly perspective on the tension between Ali’s decisive authority and the gradual, sometimes reluctant, acceptance of his counsel by the army, particularly regarding the arbitration (Hukm) that followed. The imagery of 'noon of tomorrow' suggests that true clarity often arrives only after the event has unfolded, reflecting on the human tendency to grasp wisdom retrospectively.
